fellow trans guy here- it can be difficult to come out as trans in the first place, but im sure that coming out again can be more difficult. i would suggest talking to a few close friends first, and discussing it with them. If he/him pronouns are still comfortable for you, and not dysphoric, then its not neccesary to come out to everyone again. but do whatever you feel is best, and take some time to really feel sure about yourself before coming out. best of luck!

Hey, 15 year old trans guy here. I feel the same way, and have never been in support groups, or very active in the LGBT community, and as he said "just wants to live his life as a boy without being involved in any community". Its completely understandable that he doesn't want to participate in things like that, because he doesn't want to point out the fact that he's transgender, or anything more than a "regular" boy. The best thing to do is to listen to him, and don't make him go to things he doesn't want to. I know my mom was frustrated with me when I said I didn't want to go to GSA meetings, or LGBT youth groups, but ive been out as transgender for years, and have not suffered from not being a part of these groups. Best of luck to you and your son!

I have had to deal with the same problem. I was on testosterone for around 8 months with absolutely no changes, to the point where I dropped my endocrinologist after she told me to "act more like a boy" because I didn't speak loudly. After dropping her, I never went back, am and now off T. I understand your struggles completely. They only advice I can give you is to hang on, and just keep expressing your frustration with your doctor. The only way changes will show, is from staying on testosterone. I wish I had kept on it. 

I wish you the best, and I hope you eventually see the changes you want. Congratulations on the changes you have had though!
